USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

shoulder imaging — clinical pattern 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient has focal superior shoulder pain after landing directly on the shoulder. Imaging shows an elevated distal clavicle and widened coracoclavicular distance, but the humeral head remains centered on the glenoid. Which joint injury explains the deformity?

  1. Proximal humeral surgical-neck fracture
  2. Acromioclavicular separation
  3. Anterior glenohumeral dislocation
  4. Posterior glenohumeral dislocation
  5. Inferior glenohumeral dislocation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Acromioclavicular separation

The distal clavicle is displaced relative to the acromion while the glenohumeral joint remains located.

Understanding the options

Acromioclavicular separation
The distal clavicle is displaced relative to the acromion while the glenohumeral joint remains located.
Anterior glenohumeral dislocation
The humeral head lies anterior to the glenoid, commonly in a subcoracoid position. This is not the pattern specified in this case.
Posterior glenohumeral dislocation
Axillary or another appropriate orthogonal view shows the humeral head behind the glenoid; AP imaging alone may miss it. This is not the pattern specified in this case.
Inferior glenohumeral dislocation
The humeral head lies below the glenoid, often with the arm fixed overhead. This is not the pattern specified in this case.
Proximal humeral surgical-neck fracture
A fracture below the tuberosities separates the shaft from the proximal humeral segment. This is not the pattern specified in this case.
